steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Twelve hours of steam on that gauge, which is how long your Tinker works without you, so you will sleep tonight whether you like it or not. Press Open the valve on this card.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Fifty Brass Ingots from the old stock, and I would rather they became spanners than doorstops. Press the Queue work button and set fifty Brass Spanners going.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: A watched Tinker works no faster, I am told, but nobody has ever managed not to watch the first one. Keep your eye on the bench until a Brass Spanner lands.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: That canister rattling into the tray is Pip, and Pip's canisters are seldom good news. Open the Story tab and answer the letter waiting there.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Rats have been at the Row again, and a Brass Spanner is a perfectly respectable thing to hit one with. In the Loadout, press Equip beside a Brass Spanner.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Mind your Rations and come back in one piece; I have only just got this workshop aired. Press the Queue work button and choose the Rust Rat Runt.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: The rats have paid you in Crowns, and Pip would like some. Open the Exchange tab and press Pay on Pip's bill at the top. Short? Sell rat scrap at the window below; it is worth more than it smells.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: The Row will want a word with you before the day is out, and that workbench drawer still wants clearing out; my knees are older than the Boiler. Open the Story tab and see it all through.

steps.speaker: Professor Brassbuckle
steps.line: Nothing here needs watching; the Boiler and the queue keep working while you are away, and the city will have written by the time you return. Fill twelve hours with the Queue work button, then press Leave it running.
